title: For a century, journalists have had a voluntary ethics code. Editors are giving it an AI-era reboot
description: The Society of Professional Journalists is revising its Code of Ethics for the first time since 2014. The update addresses challenges like artificial intelligence, the rise of independent journalists, and an erosion of public trust in media. The code, organized around four key principles, has guided journalists for nearly a century. The revision process is lengthy, involving extensive meetings and feedback. The new draft includes a focus on accountability and ethical responsibility, regardless of technology used. The SPJ believes these updates are crucial for maintaining journalistic integrity in a rapidly changing industry.

The National Education Policy aims to tackle these evolving challenges, emphasizing the importance of parental involvement. With a large youth demographic, India holds tremendous potential for future success.
